transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-06
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Amit Shah (NexaHealth Eng Lead), Laura Gomez (Platform Ops), Samir Khan (Security)

Summary section (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Quick check of onboarding tasks, access blockers, and benchmarking plan.

00:00 Jordan: okay, hi everyone thanks for joining on time, this is Jordan from Redwood. we have Priya from our SE team too. um, today's agenda - just run through onboarding progress, any blockers for environment prep, and align on the benchmark runs.
00:12 Amit: yeah thanks Jordan, morning. quick context - we've got infra team standing by but need to lock down peering window and keys.
00:20 Priya: great, can you remind me which AWS account we'll be using for the test? I think last week you mentioned a separate test account?
00:28 Laura: yes, we spun up a sandbox account in us-west-2, it's "nexa-sandbox-2027". but we haven't given any cross-account roles yet, that's the blocker.
00:36 Jordan: ok got it. so for the hosted benchmark we can run without peering, we just need API keys and a sample dataset. for private deployment / VPC we'll need peering and IAM roles and KMS access.
00:49 Amit: perfect. on the API keys, we want to avoid sending production data; we'll use subset of anonymized records. what does Redwood need for KMS access if we decide to test private?
00:58 Priya: for KMS we need to be able to encrypt/decrypt model cache blobs if you host keys customer-managed. usually we ask for a key policy that allows the Redwood service principal to use the key. Samir, that probably ties into your compliance reqs.
01:10 Samir: yeah we have strict policy around key access. we won't add wide perms; we'll want least-privilege, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. also SSO/SAML must be in place for console access.
01:20 Jordan: totally. Jordan: we'll send a sample key policy and the SOC2 docs. should help short-circuit review.
01:27 Amit: cool. quick operational question - for the benchmark we want latency at 512 tokens and 1k tokens, can Redwood report p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens?
01:36 Priya: yes we will. priya: we'll run p50/p95, throughput QPS, and estimated cost per 1k tokens for the sample prompt set. we'll also include configuration: batch size, sequence len, quantization profile.
01:47 Laura: that would be helpful. also can you include model variant fallback behaviour when capacity is constrained?
01:53 Priya: yes we'll note fallback options; by default hosted falls back to compatible variants we pre-approve. we can document exact model mapping for your prompt set.
02:02 Amit: any idea about expected perf for a 7B-qty quantized model vs full fp16 on A10G? just rough numbers, looking for order of magnitude.
02:12 Priya: rough yes - quantized 4-bit runs can give 2-3x cost reduction with modest latency increase in some cases; fp16 on A10G lower latency but higher cost. we'll put real numbers after we run the hosted run.
02:24 Jordan: and remember we can also do KV/prefix cache to reduce repeated prefix cost for chat use-cases. that often drops per-request tokens significantly.
02:33 Amit: good note.
02:36 Laura: on networking, infra needs the VPC CIDR and peering proposal, what's the typical peering setup?
02:42 Priya: we usually ask for a VPC peering connection from your VPC to Redwood's customer-dedicated VPC, or optionally an AWS Transit Gateway. we will send a recommendation doc. if you prefer private deployment on-prem we can discuss offline.
02:54 Amit: right, for now we just want to get the sandbox running with hosted benchmark; peering is for later.
03:00 Jordan: ok so immediate path: hosted benchmark first, then private/dedicated POC if you want to push it behind VPC.
03:06 Samir: quick security Q - how do you handle audit logs and retention?
03:10 Priya: we push request/response metadata to audit logs (configurable), and we can integrate with your SIEM via forwarder. retention is a config, and for private deployments we can keep logs in customer-owned S3 with lifecycle policies.
03:21 Samir: good. also what about token-level redaction or PII scrubbing?
03:25 Jordan: we don't modify customer input by default; we can enable rules or pipeline to scrub PII before sending to model, or you can do that pre-ingest in your side. we'll share patterns we've seen.
03:35 Amit: perfect. on the sample prompt set - who will own that?
03:39 Jordan: Redwood can supply a starter set based on clinical triage examples, but we'll need you to add typical edge cases. Priya will share the starter list.
03:47 Priya: yes I'll drop the prompt pack after this call. it's a small JSONL with 50 prompts covering short/long sequences.
03:53 Laura: and for the benchmark run, what's the timeline?
03:56 Priya: I'm free to run the hosted benchmark tomorrow if you can provide the anonymized dataset and API test creds by EOD. otherwise earliest Wed morning.
04:06 Amit: I can get creds to you by tomorrow noon. we just need to coordinate with infra.
04:11 Jordan: great. moving on - any blockers on SSO?
04:14 Samir: we haven't finished SAML config for the sandbox account. that might block console access but API access still possible.
04:20 Jordan: API access is enough for the benchmark. console access we'll handle later.
04:24 Amit: one more thing - can Redwood provide an estimated cost for a month-long pilot if we go with Dedicated reserved capacity? we need ballpark for procurement.
04:33 Jordan: yes we'll produce a ballpark; Jordan: I'll follow up with a simple compare table: hosted pay-as-you-go vs dedicated monthly commit with expected throughput.
04:42 Laura: great, procurement will need that too.
04:46 Priya: also a note on tuning - often we suggest increasing batch sizes slightly for throughput-sensitive endpoints, but if latency SLO is tight we pick smaller batches and low-latency kernels. we'll include config examples.
04:57 Amit: ok awesome. any demo requests for next week?
05:01 Laura: maybe a short demo on KV cache and prefix caching, that helps our product folks.
05:06 Jordan: noted - we'll schedule 30m KV cache demo.
05:10 Priya: and for the security deep-dive we'll invite our compliance engineer.
05:14 Jordan: recap / next steps: Jordan to send SOC2 + network diagram, Priya to share runbook and prompt pack, customer to provide IAM creds and VPC CIDR, schedule security deep-dive for next Tue.
05:27 Amit: thanks all, that works.
05:30 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links. bye.
